scene.note: One scrawled entry no longer stops the night's total, and a real mistake still reaches the code that called.

steps.note: A text from the log arrives, with a fallback to use if it is not a whole number.
A text that is not a whole number is expected, and gives the fallback.
Anything else that goes wrong, such as no text at all, travels on to the code that called.
One entry arrives and is taken apart at its semicolon.
Only turning the hours into a number may fail quietly.
An entry that cannot be taken apart is not a callout, and its error reaches the caller.
The whole log arrives, entry by entry.
Hours that can be read are added to the total.
Each entry that cannot be read is kept with the message of its error.
Ailsa gets the total and the entries to ask about.
Ailsa asks for the log of a night, by its path.
A night with no log file gives empty text instead of a traceback.
A path that is a folder is a real mistake, and its error reaches the caller.
